record.title: The shuffle-chain conjecture
record.statement: Fix integers $d\geq 2$ and $p\geq 1$. Let a **$p$-shuffle chain** be the tree-valued Markov chain described in the paper, whose transitions rearrange subtrees branching from a chosen length-$p$ ancestral path. **The shuffle-chain conjecture.** There exists an integer $k_0(d,p)$ such that, for every $k\geq k_0(d,p)$, there is a $p$-shuffle chain on $\mathcal{C}_k^{(d)}$ whose stationary distribution is uniform on $\mathcal{C}_k^{(d)}$. This is presented as a Markov-chain formulation related to subtree shuffling; the source does not report a resolution.
record.source_name: Elia Bisi, Piotr Dyszewski, Nina Gantert, Samuel G. G. Johnston, Joscha Prochno and Dominik Schmid, “Random planar trees and the Jacobian conjecture”, arXiv:2301.08221 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.08221

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2023).

record.title: Unbounded envelope heights for finite subsets
record.statement: Let $\str H$ and $\str G$ be the structures in the source, let $\varphi\colon\str H\to\str G$ be an embedding, and let an envelope of a finite subset have the source's valuation-tree meaning. Assume that for every $n\in\omega$ there is $a\in\omega$ such that the number of relations of arity $a$ is at least $n$. **Unbounded envelope-height conjecture.** For every embedding $\varphi\colon\str H\to\str G$, there is some $k\in\omega$ such that for every $R\in\omega$ there is a set $S\subseteq\varphi[\str H]$ with $|S|=k$ whose every envelope has height at least $R$. This strengthens the claim that no single embedding is uniformly $k$-enveloping.
record.source_name: Samuel Braunfeld, David Chodounský, Noé de Rancourt, Jan Hubička, Jamal Kawach and Matěj Konečný, “Big Ramsey Degrees and Infinite Languages”, arXiv:2301.13116 (2024).

record.title: Wrochna's topological Hedetniemi conjecture for free involutive complexes
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{K}$ and $\mathcal{L}$ be finite free $\mathbb Z/2$-simplicial complexes, with diagonal action on their Cartesian product, and let $\operatorname{ind} X$ denote the least $k$ for which there is a $\mathbb Z/2$-equivariant map from $X$ to $E_k(\mathbb Z/2)$. **Wrochna's topological Hedetniemi conjecture.** For every such pair,

$$
\operatorname{ind}(\mathcal{K}\times\mathcal{L})=\min\{\operatorname{ind}\mathcal{K},\operatorname{ind}\mathcal{L}\}.
$$
 This is the equivariant-space analogue of Hedetniemi's graph conjecture, which has been disproved; the status of this topological formulation is not settled by the supplied text.
record.source_name: Vuong Bui and Hamid Reza Daneshpajouh, “A topological version of Hedetniemi's conjecture for equivariant spaces”, arXiv:2302.06178 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.06178

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2023). “However, there are still some interesting open questions around.”

record.title: Finiteness conjecture for k-dicritical semi-complete digraphs
record.statement: A **semi-complete digraph** is a digraph in which every pair of distinct vertices is joined by at least one directed arc. **Semi-complete-digraph finiteness conjecture.** For every $k\geq4$, there are only finitely many $k$-dicritical semi-complete digraphs. The paper proves finiteness and characterizes the 3-dicritical semi-complete case, and presents this statement as a challenge for general $k\geq4$; the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Frédéric Havet, Florian Hörsch and Lucas Picasarri-Arrieta, “The 3-dicritical semi-complete digraphs”, arXiv:2402.12014 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.12014

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

record.title: Aubian et al.'s universal dijoin strictness conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\ell\geq 3$. **Aubian et al.'s conjecture.** There exists an oriented graph $D_1$ with $\operatorname{inv}(D_1)=\ell$ such that, for every oriented graph $D_2$ with $\operatorname{inv}(D_2)\geq 1$, 
$$
\operatorname{inv}(D_1\rightarrow D_2)<\operatorname{inv}(D_1)+\operatorname{inv}(D_2).
$$
 This is the stronger of the two related conjectures discussed in the source: one fixed graph of each inversion number at least three should force strict subadditivity against every non-acyclic factor.
record.source_name: Natalie Behague, Tom Johnston, Natasha Morrison and Shannon Ogden, “A note on inverting the dijoin of oriented graphs”, arXiv:2404.10663 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10663

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

record.title: The consecutive Davenport constant conjecture for finite groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, and let ${\sf C}(G)$ denote its consecutive Davenport constant, namely the least length $\ell$ such that every sequence of $ell$ elements of $G$ contains a nonempty consecutive product-one subsequence.

**Consecutive Davenport constant conjecture.** For every finite group $G$, it holds

$$
{\sf C}(G)=|G|.
$$

The equality is established in the source for finite abelian groups and metacyclic groups, as well as for direct products of a finite abelian group with a metacyclic group. The general case remains open.
record.source_name: A. Lemos, A. O. Moura, S. Ribas and A. T. Silva, “A note on weighted consecutive Davenport constant”, arXiv:2404.11312 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.11312

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

record.title: Aubian et al.'s universal counterexample conjecture for dijoin inversion
record.statement:
Let $L$ and $R$ be oriented graphs, let $L\Rightarrow R$ denote their dijoin, and let $\operatorname{inv}(D)$ denote the inversion number of an oriented graph $D$.

**Aubian et al.'s conjecture.** For every integer $k\ge 3$, there exists a tournament $T_k$ with

$$
\operatorname{inv}(T_k)=k
$$

such that, for every oriented graph $R$ with $\operatorname{inv}(R)\ge 1$,

$$
\operatorname{inv}(T_k\Rightarrow R)<k+\operatorname{inv}(R).
$$

The claim extends Aubian et al.'s proved construction for odd $k\ge3$ to all $k\ge3$; the supplied text gives no resolution of the even case.
record.source_name: Haozhe Wang, Yuxuan Yang and Mei Lu, “The inversion number of dijoins and blow-up digraphs”, arXiv:2404.14937 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.14937

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

record.title: Chromatic invariance conjecture for generalized Sierpiński gasket graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph, let $t$ be a positive integer, and let $S[G,t]$ denote the generalized Sierpiński gasket graph based on $G$ at level $t$. Write $\chi(G)$ for the chromatic number of $G$. **Chromatic invariance conjecture.** For each graph $G$ and each integer $t\geq 1$, 
$$
\chi\left(S[G,t]\right)=\chi(G).
$$
 The paper proves this equality for $t=1,2$, for bipartite graphs, and gives the bound $\chi(G)\leq\chi(S[G,t])\leq\chi(G)+1$ for $t\geq3$; the conjecture remains open in the supplied text for arbitrary graphs and all $t\geq1$.
record.source_name: Fatemeh Attarzadeh, Ahmad Abbasi and Ali Behtoei, “Chromatic and Clique number of Generalized Sierpiński Gasket Graph S[G,t]”, arXiv:2405.19172 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.19172

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

record.title: The eventual monotonicity conjecture for minimal subword entropy
record.statement:
For $k \geq 2$, let $\min S_{\mathrm{sw}}^{(k)}(n)$ denote the minimal subword entropy among words of length $n$. **Eventual monotonicity conjecture.** There is a value $N$ such that the function

$$
\frac{\min S_{\mathrm{sw}}^{(k)}(n)}{n}
$$

is increasing for $n \geq N$.

The function is known experimentally not to be increasing for all $n$, so the conjecture asserts only eventual monotonicity. Its general status is open.
record.source_name: Wenjie Fang, “Maximal number of subword occurrences in a word”, arXiv:2406.02971 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.02971

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

record.title: Product-one subsequence conjecture for the ordered Davenport constant
record.statement:
For a finite group $G$, let $\mathsf{D}(G)$ be the least positive integer such that every sequence of that length over $G$ has a nonempty product-one subsequence, and let $\mathsf{E}(G)$ be the least integer $k$ such that every sequence of length $k$ over $G$ has a product-one ordered subsequence of length $|G|$. The **ordered Davenport constant conjecture.** One has

$$
\mathsf{E}(G)=\mathsf{D}(G)+|G|-1.
$$

For finite abelian groups this equality is known, while the source establishes the lower bound $\mathsf{E}(G)\geq\mathsf{D}(G)+|G|-1$ for finite non-abelian groups. The conjecture asks whether equality holds for every finite group.
record.source_name: Naveen K. Godara, Renu Joshi and Eshita Mazumdar, “An algebraic approach towards a conjecture on the Davenport constant”, arXiv:2407.01148 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.01148

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

record.title: Jerebic's eventual non-distance-balancedness conjecture for generalized Petersen graphs
record.statement:
Let $n\ge 3$ and $1\le k<n/2$. The **generalized Petersen graph** $GP(n,k)$ has vertex set

$$
V(GP(n,k))=\\{u_i:i\in\mathbb{Z}_n\\}\cup\\{v_i:i\in\mathbb{Z}_n\\}
$$

and edge set

$$
E(GP(n,k))=\\{u_iu_{i+1}:i\in\mathbb{Z}_n\\}\cup\\{v_iv_{i+k}:i\in\mathbb{Z}_n\\}\cup\\{u_iv_i:i\in\mathbb{Z}_n\\}.
$$

**Jerebic's conjecture.** For any $k\ge 2$, there exists a positive integer $n_0$ such that $GP(n,k)$ is not distance-balanced for every $n\ge n_0$. The conjecture was positively resolved by Yang et al.; in fact, if $k\ge 2$ and $n>6k^2$, then $GP(n,k)$ is not distance-balanced.
record.source_name: Gang Ma, Jianfeng Wang and Sandi Klavžar, “On \1,2\-distance-balancedness of generalized Petersen graphs”, arXiv:2407.02635 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.02635

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2024). “The conjecture has been positively resolved by Yang et al.\ as follows.”

record.title: Power-of-two periodicity conjecture for pattern-avoidance counts
record.statement:
Let $f_n^k(\sigma)$ denote the number of permutations of length $n$ associated with a pattern $\sigma\in S_3$ and fixed by the $k$th iterate of the fundamental bijection. **Power-of-two periodicity conjecture.** For $i,j\geq2$, $n\geq1$, and $\sigma\in S_3$,

$$
f_n^{2^i}(\sigma)=f_n^{2^j}(\sigma).
$$

This conjecture proposes that all iterates whose exponents are powers of two with exponent at least two give the same count for every length and every pattern in $S_3$; the supplied text gives no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Kassie Archer and Robert P. Laudone, “Pattern avoidance and the fundamental bijection”, arXiv:2407.06338 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.06338

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

record.title: The spacing-five conjecture for critical prism-canvases
record.statement:
A **prism-canvas** is a cylindrical fragment $(F,T_1,T_2,L)$ whose boundary faces are bounded by triangles $T_1,T_2$, with $|L(v)|\geq 5$ for every vertex outside the boundary triangles; it is **critical** when $F$ is $(T_1\cup T_2)$-critical with respect to $L$. Its **spacing** is the distance between the boundary triangles in the cylindrical fragment.

**The spacing-five conjecture.** There is no critical prism-canvas of spacing at least five.

A theorem cited in the paper gives an absolute upper bound on the spacing of critical prism-canvases, but the source notes that the explicit bound is much larger and presents spacing at least five as a conjectural strengthening.
record.source_name: Zdeněk Dvořák and Félix Moreno Peñarrubia, “Towards Characterization of 5-List-Colorability of Toroidal Graphs”, arXiv:2407.18800 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.18800

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

record.title: The unbounded attacking-cop-number gap conjecture
record.statement:
For a graph $G$, let $\operatorname{c}(G)$ denote its cop number and let $\operatorname{cc}(G)$ denote its attacking cop number. Let $k$ range over the non-negative integers.

**Unbounded attacking-cop-number gap conjecture.** For every non-negative integer $k$, there exists a graph $H$ such that

$$
\operatorname{cc}(H)-\operatorname{c}(H)\geq k.
$$

This conjecture asserts that the gap between attacking cop number and cop number is unbounded. The source gives no resolution; it notes that constructing examples with gap at least $2$ has been nontrivial.
record.source_name: Alexander Clow, Melissa A. Huggan and M. E. Messinger, “Cops and Attacking Robbers with Cycle Constraints”, arXiv:2408.02225 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.02225

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2024).

record.title: Strongly self-dual graph realization conjecture for Reuleaux polyhedra
record.statement: A planar, 3-connected graph $G$ is **strongly self-dual** if it has a self-duality isomorphism $\tau:G\to G^*$ such that, for every pair of vertices $u,v$, $u\in\tau(v)$ if and only if $v\in\tau(u)$, and no vertex satisfies $u\in\tau(u)$. A **Reuleaux polyhedron** is a ball-polyhedron in $\mathbb{E}^3$, that is, an intersection of finitely many unit balls, with each center and each vertex corresponding to the other. **Strongly self-dual realization conjecture.** For every planar, 3-connected, strongly self-dual graph $G$, there is a Reuleaux polyhedron in $\mathbb{E}^3$ whose edge graph is isomorphic to $G$. A weaker realization result provides a possibly non-injective point assignment; injectivity is equivalent to the conjecture, which the source identifies as open.
record.source_name: Károly Bezdek, Zsolt Lángi and Márton Naszódi, “Selected topics from the theory of intersections of balls”, arXiv:2411.10302 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.10302

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2024). “Surprisingly, Problem is still open in $\Ee^2$. In fact, Alexander conjectured that under any contraction of the center points of a finite family of unit disks in the plane, the perimeter of the intersection does not decrease.”

record.title: The family-level tower lower-bound conjecture for tightly connected hypergraphs
record.statement:
For integers $k$ and $s$, let $\mathcal{H}_s^{(k)}$ be the family of $s$-tightly connected $k$-graphs that are not $k$-partite. A hypergraph is **$s$-tightly connected** if any two edges can be joined by a sequence of edges in which consecutive edges share at least $s$ vertices. Define the tower function by

$$
t_1(x)=x,\qquad t_i(x)=2^{t_{i-1}(x)}\quad\text{for all }i\geq 2.
$$

**The family-level tower lower-bound conjecture.** If $k>s$, then there exists a positive constant $c$ such that

$$
r(\mathcal{H}_s^{(k)},K_n^{(k)})\geq t_s(n^c).
$$

This is explicitly proposed as a stronger version of the corresponding conjecture for each individual tightly connected hypergraph. It remains open.
record.source_name: David Conlon, Jacob Fox, Benjamin Gunby, Xiaoyu He, Dhruv Mubayi, Andrew Suk, Jacques Verstraëte and Hung-Hsun Hans Yu, “When are off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey numbers polynomial?”, arXiv:2411.13812 (2025).

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2024).

record.title: The strong Diophantine conjecture on bounded continued fractions
record.statement:
Let $t,u$ be positive integers with $t<u$ and $\gcd(t,u)=1$. Consider continued-fraction expansions of the form

$$
\frac{t}{u}=[b_1,1,b_2,1,\ldots,b_m,1],
$$

where $b_1,\ldots,b_m\geq 1$. **Diophantine conjecture.** There is a universal constant $A>0$ such that, for every integer $t\geq 3$, there is a coprime integer $u>t$ for which the quotient $t/u$ has such an expansion with $b_1,\ldots,b_m\leq A$. This conjecture would imply the logarithmic upper-bound conjecture for planar spanning-tree numbers via the paper's Main Graph Theorem. It remains unproved, while the paper establishes it for a set of positive proportion of integers $t$.
record.source_name: Swee Hong Chan, Alex Kontorovich and Igor Pak, “Spanning trees and continued fractions”, arXiv:2411.18782 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.18782

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2024).

record.title: Goddyn's thin tree conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be an unweighted undirected graph. A set $T\subseteq E$ is **$\alpha$-thin** with respect to $G$ if, for every nonempty set $S\subsetneq V$,

$$
\lvert T(S,\overline{S})\rvert\leq\alpha\lvert E(S,\overline{S})\rvert.
$$

A graph is $d$-edge-connected if every cut has at least $d$ edges. **Thin Tree Conjecture.** For any $\alpha<1$, there exists $d\geq1$ such that any $d$-edge-connected graph $G$ has a spanning tree $T$ that is $\alpha$-thin. This conjecture asks for combinatorial constructions of thin spanning trees; spectral constructions of linear-sized thin subsets are known, but the combinatorial question remains open.
record.source_name: Shayan Oveis Gharan and Arvin Sahami, “Unweighted One-Sided Code Sparsifiers and Thin Subgraphs”, arXiv:2502.02799 (2025).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2024–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2403.05178](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.05178).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.02799

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2025). “We remark that there has been a "spectral" constructions of linear-sized thin subsets, see, e.g., but it remained an open problem whether one can construct thin subsets combinatorially without appealing to linear algebraic arguments.”

record.title: Füredi's 4-CM conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, and let a **connected matching** be a matching whose distinct edges have adjacent endpoint sets. **Füredi's 4-CM conjecture.** For every integer $t\geqslant1$, every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G)=2$ and at least $4t-1$ vertices has a connected matching of size at least 
$$
t.
$$
 The bound $4t-1$ is best possible, but the conjecture remains an asserted strengthening in the paper.
record.source_name: Jofre Costa, Eric Luu, David R. Wood and Jung Hon Yip, “Verifying Hadwiger's Conjecture for Examples of Graphs with α(G) = 2”, arXiv:2512.17114 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17114

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

record.title: Type 1 conjecture for fullerene nanodiscs
record.statement: A **fullerene nanodisc** $D_r$ is a fullerene nanodisc indexed by an integer $r$. **Type 1 conjecture.** The fullerene nanodiscs $D_r$, for every integer $r\geq 2$, are Type 1. The conjecture would classify the entire family of fullerene nanodiscs with indices at least $2$ as Type 1, extending the paper's result for $r=5+3k$ with $k\in\mathbb{Z}^{+}$ and supporting Brinkmann, Preissmann and Sasaki's conjecture.
